title: Arijit Singh Announces Nine-City India Tour To Mark 20 Years In Music
excerpt: Playback singer Arijit Singh will tour nine Indian cities from January to May 2027, marking 20 years in music with stadium-scale shows billed as the largest live production of his career at home.
body:
• The Arijit Singh India Tour 2027 runs Jan. 9 through May 15, 2027, hitting Ahmedabad, Chandigarh, Jaipur, Mumbai, Bengaluru, New Delhi, Pune, Indore, and Hyderabad.
  • Tickets sell exclusively on thumpN. A Kotak Solitaire Visa credit card presale opens Oct. 10 at 12 pm; a second Kotak Visa cardholder presale runs Oct. 11 from 12 pm; general sales begin Oct. 13 at 2 pm.
  • The stadium-scale shows promise a multi-tiered stage with an extended runway, 360-degree spatial audio, kinetic LED fixtures, panoramic screens, laser arrays, and pyrotechnics — described by promoters as the largest-scale live production of Singh's career in India.
  • This is Singh's first major India run since he announced he was stepping away from film playback singing, and it marks 20 years since he entered the music industry.

A 20-Year Celebration on the Biggest Possible Stage

Playback singer Arijit Singh has announced the Arijit Singh India Tour 2027, a nine-city, stadium-scale concert run that will mark two decades since he entered the music industry. Presented by Kotak Solitaire and produced and promoted by Team Innovation, the tour kicks off Jan. 9, 2027, in Ahmedabad and closes May 15 in Hyderabad, with stops in Chandigarh (Jan. 23), Jaipur (Feb. 7), Mumbai (Feb. 20), Bengaluru (March 13), New Delhi (March 27), Pune (April 10), and Indore (May 1).

In a statement released with the announcement, Singh framed the run as a homecoming rather than a victory lap: "20 years of music is a journey I feel very grateful for. The greatest part of it has always been the people – the listeners who have given these songs a life of their own. I'm really looking forward to travelling across India and experiencing that love together, live on stage. There are so many songs, so many memories and so many people to meet. I can't wait."

"20 years of music is a journey I feel very grateful for. The greatest part of it has always been the people – the listeners who have given these songs a life of their own."

— Arijit Singh

Context & Background

Singh, widely regarded as India's most streamed artist across several years, built his career on ballads that became generational fixtures — "Tum Hi Ho," "Channa Mereya," "Phir Le Aya Dil," "Qaafirana," and more recently "Gehra Hua." The announcement lands months after his decision to step away from the film music industry as a playback singer, a move that prompted industry-wide speculation about his future. A handful of film songs have continued to surface since — "Jai Jai Ram" from Ramayana: Part 1 composed by A.R. Rahman with Shreya Ghoshal, "Purane Din" for Pehla Pyaar Doosri Baar, and "Yeh Awarapan" for Awarapan 2 — but this tour is his first major India run since that announcement, and it appears to pivot him toward the independent live stage.

Mohit Bijlani, founder of Team Innovation, called the tour "a genuine tribute to an extraordinary musical legacy," adding that every detail was being designed to "world-class standards" to deliver a live experience at a scale not seen before in Singh's home country.

Impact & Analysis

The production design signals how far India's concert economy has come. The shows will feature a custom-built multi-tiered stage with an extended runway so Singh can move deeper into the crowd, along with 360-degree spatial audio, kinetic LED fixtures, panoramic screens, laser arrays, and stadium-scale pyrotechnics. That is a specification sheet that would be at home on a global pop act's stadium itinerary — and it reflects a domestic live-music market that has grown dramatically in scale and ambition over the last five years.

Positioning also matters: nine cities across five months suggests Team Innovation is betting that demand for Singh's catalogue — spanning languages, generations, and film eras — can fill stadiums, not just arenas. If these shows sell out on the reported scale, the tour will set a benchmark for Indian artists as live draws in their home market rather than primarily abroad.

Diaspora Angle

Singh's overseas tours have historically played to packed houses of Indian diaspora audiences, from London's arenas to North American amphitheatres. This tour, India-only so far, underscores how the centre of gravity for Indian music's biggest live draws is shifting homeward. For diaspora fans, the immediate takeaway is practical: this itinerary covers only Indian cities, and with ticket sales restricted to the thumpN platform, planning travel around a specific date — Ahmedabad's Jan. 9 opener or Hyderabad's May 15 finale, for instance — would need to start soon.

What's Next

Venues for individual shows have not yet been announced, and further details are expected as dates approach. The setlist is expected to span different phases of Singh's career, pairing enduring film favourites with newer material. For now, the three presale windows in October are the critical calendar items: miss the Kotak presales and general sales open Oct. 13 — Team Innovation has promised an announcement cadence that will reveal show-level details city by city.
